$comment: Supported Foundry-Edge pairing, metadata version 2. qualification records hosted pairing acceptance separately from actual Foundry publication and verified Edge distribution. Immutable v0.4.0, v0.5.0, v0.5.1, v0.5.2, v0.5.3, v0.5.4, v0.5.5 and v0.5.6 release records are under docs/release-notes/. CI reads edge.image; docs/compatibility.md records the support envelope, including the starter production identity path first qualified in v0.5.6.

edge.build: published release v0.9.21; verified distribution at f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3. Foundry v0.5.7 candidate qualification and publication are pending; prior release evidence does not qualify this pairing

requirements: It retains ferrum-edge#5661 conditional writes, ferrum-edge#4611 proxy association, and namespace-qualified resource identity (ferrum-edge 5db1d77a8, aligned in #409). The qualification checks these contracts against the published release.

GET /proxies/{id}/mcp/tools remains a viewer-readable, namespace-scoped MCP catalog read; viewer-key namespace ceilings apply to every namespace route and deny global routes outside the documented allowlist. Capability parity includes the new read route.

Operator reads of upstreams mask the Consul ACL token, and operator reads of plugin configs mask secrets, credential-bearing endpoint URL components, TLS private-key material, destination paths, and trigger header/query/cookie operands, with redaction placeholders. A POST or PUT of a proxy, upstream, or plugin config that echoes a placeholder at a masked field (or the reserved [REDACTED] literal in a non-admin plugin config) is refused with 400 before update merging (ferrum-edge#5925, #7054, #7060), so for upstreams and plugin configs a placeholder is not a round-trip marker; admin-only consumer credential entries still round-trip [REDACTED]. Admin reads are raw and never refused. Foundry's editors block such a save, for a non-admin role and only at the sites Edge masks, until each field is re-entered or cleared.

Ferrum Edge v0.9.21 (published 2026-11-22) is the latest Edge release. It adds non-admin TLS-material and trigger-operand redaction and exact [REDACTED] reservation (ferrum-edge#7054, #7060), consumer credential If-Match preconditions (ferrum-edge#7393), external_identity and external_identity_authority trigger predicates (ferrum-edge#7417), removes pool_max_requests_per_connection (#7218) and mcp_gateway discovery.hide_denied_items (#7136), and enforces cleartext non-loopback refusal on request_mirror (#6659). Its publication is not a claim that all upstream security issues are fixed.

Plugin-config PUT and DELETE require the expected_proxy_ids association precondition (ferrum-edge-git-forge-ops#569, ferrum-edge#6744, first published in v0.9.19); Foundry's membership plan already sends it, and a write that would detach a proxy outside the expected set is refused with 412. An admin token's ns claim always bounds its authority (ferrum-edge#6093): Foundry's BFF namespace route ceiling already matches it, and scoped /health and /status answer the tenant tier, which projectHealthSummary reduces. Gateway material references remain default-deny for namespace-claimed operators (ferrum-edge#6092 residual). Consumer credential floors and uniqueness checks from v0.9.19+ remain enforced, and indexed credential delete now honors If-Match against the consumer ETag (ferrum-edge#7393).

Foundry v0.5.7 retains guarded-write policy #542, first shipped in v0.5.2 (#544): guarded replacement and deletion refuse an initial fresh verification read without one nonempty quoted visible-ASCII strong ETag, before any PUT/DELETE. Explicit unguarded calls, low-level helpers and plugin membership plans keep their semantics, and the post-412 untagged refusal is unchanged. The paired release issues strong item ETags, so qualification must show every guarded editor write still succeeds against it.

Static guided-schema review at f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3: KeyAuthConfig, CorsConfig and PrometheusMetricsConfig are byte-identical to e4a606a00352674daaef08636e3e359e6c48ba18. RateLimitingConfig removes the redundant default keyword on redis_key_prefix while retaining the same prose default (digest d378b0338ce52c2664bb9bc968e42adb344a08db59b46966ba5255f0498da5f4). RateLimitingRuleConfig updates the unmodelled consumers field description to state mapped Consumer username matching only (digest d173852f113c1823ee6231478cea929e2c915c77b778ff4abc8015dec1e270b0). PLUGIN_SCHEMA_SPEC.ref moves to f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3. SubsetTrafficPolicy is byte-identical to e4a606a00352674daaef08636e3e359e6c48ba18 and SUBSET_TRAFFIC_POLICY_SOURCE moves to f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3. The sensitivity source changes (Git blob d50b0d53b7a4ace7454a25a7e8034b4a8ea5c1a8 to 5f96f581ead10e8c777fc088fda10ffe89c96b6d): 16 plugins gain rules (request_termination, transaction_debugger, ai_semantic_firewall, waf, openapi_validator, ai_tool_governor, mcp_gateway, opa, mesh_route_dispatch, request_mirror, mtls_auth, soap_ws_security, udp_logging, mesh_authz, plus redis_url on jwks_auth, hmac_auth, and soap_ws_security), and Foundry's table and PLUGIN_SENSITIVITY_SOURCE follow at f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3.

Published contracts-edge-0.9.20 at 39da322083044c2e92617209e62983c92387f0ad remains pinned pending publication of contracts-edge-0.9.21 in ferrum-edge/ferrum-contracts. Edge v0.9.21 retains the same 82 built-in plugins, priorities, stream protocol matrix, and provisioned-by attribution as v0.9.20; re-vendor contracts-edge-0.9.21 once published.

Qualification is pending. The full qualification must be re-run with edge.image moved to that release, and every job is green on the main push run, before any Foundry release is published: Qualification Source, Quality Gate on Node 22 and 24, Pinned Gateway Contract (including capability parity, writable and read-only), Deployment Starter, Starter Production Profile, Critical Journeys, Container Gate (amd64), and Container Gate (arm64).

edge_dependencies.what: strong ETag on resource reads and If-Match on PUT/DELETE of proxies, upstreams, consumers, and plugin configs; a malformed If-Match, or one on a route that does not evaluate it, is 400
edge_dependencies.status: first released in Ferrum Edge v0.9.7; retained in Ferrum Edge v0.9.8, v0.9.9, v0.9.10, v0.9.11, v0.9.12, v0.9.13, v0.9.14, v0.9.15, v0.9.17, v0.9.19, v0.9.20, and v0.9.21
edge_dependencies.effect_on_pinned_edge: Foundry's write guard sends If-Match with the ETag of its verification read, so a writer that commits between that read and the write is refused with 412; the gateway contract asserts the 412s and the 400s

edge_dependencies.what: optional proxy_id filter on GET /plugins/config (exact match, paginated over the filtered set, invalid value is 400)
edge_dependencies.status: first released in Ferrum Edge v0.9.7; retained in Ferrum Edge v0.9.8, v0.9.9, v0.9.10, v0.9.11, v0.9.12, v0.9.13, v0.9.14, v0.9.15, v0.9.17, v0.9.19, v0.9.20, and v0.9.21
edge_dependencies.effect_on_pinned_edge: a proxy's Plugins tab lists the proxy-scoped configurations targeting it from the filtered collection instead of the whole namespace; a response the filter did not narrow is refused rather than shown

edge_dependencies.what: PUT and DELETE of /plugins/config/{id} require the expected_proxy_ids association precondition (an empty value expects none; absent or malformed is 400); a write that would detach a referencing proxy outside that set is refused with 412, atomically with the write (ferrum-edge-git-forge-ops#569)
edge_dependencies.status: tagged in Ferrum Edge v0.9.18, which was not published; released in Ferrum Edge v0.9.19, v0.9.20, and v0.9.21
edge_dependencies.effect_on_pinned_edge: Foundry's membership plan sends the proxies its own reads showed referencing the configuration, so a proxy another writer attached after that read is refused with 412 instead of being silently detached
